themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture next to a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: On generative content review all three models warn that separately approved claims can combine into a false message and that tone and paraphrase change liability, and on the shared meaning layer for agents they call conflicting definitions of "active customer" a political settlement rather than a data model.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own from cases they already know for certain.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization the models say stochastic, personalized answers leave no stable baseline; on identity resolution they recruit a consenting panel because nobody knows who is really the same person; on incrementality the platform changes while you measure it; and on content review the models start by mining past rejections.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution every model puts a proxy or gateway in front of martech writes with hard spend and audience caps, on downstream consent they funnel every data exit through a single checkpoint, and on journey orchestration they build one shared contact log that can only say no.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. So the models try to make honesty pay: a faster lane, a better price, a perk for whoever declares themselves.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models build declared-agent checkout lanes and discounts rather than detection, on journey orchestration they note channel owners are paid to keep sending, and on incrementality they say platforms have no reason to expose auditable treatment assignment.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and guess whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three models say a person cannot be unlearned from a trained model and black-box ad platforms give no read-back, and on safe agent execution they note vendor APIs expose no rollback or agent identity to check against.
